catalog_quote: [Yang, Yang & O'Grady 2019, p. 21(-22), Google Books search-within-volume snippet:] ... vowel length, stress, and tone are not used contrastively in Modern Jejueo. Moreover, Jejueo is prosodically somewhat similar to the Seoul variety of Korean, with accentual phrases whose basic tonal pattern is Low-High-Low-High (S.-H. Lee 2014). However, there are also ... [Saltzman 2022, pp. 59-60, open text:] The other dialect areas have distinctive tone, like Hamgyeong, distinctive vowel length like the Central dialects, or both, like Gyeongsang. The Hwanghae dialect and Jejueo are distinctive in having neither pitch accent nor long vowels (King 2006 and Yeon 2012).

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both quoted passages are verbatim in copies we hold at the stated locators (Google Books PA21 snippet JSONs; Saltzman 2022 txt at the p.59/60 break). (2) The deciding source is the right one: Yang, Yang & O'Grady 2020 is the standard and only full reference grammar of Jejueo (Glottolog rank 'grammar', xii+302 pp), and the statement sits in its phonology chapter (ch.2, pp.15-36). The weakness is custody, not choice: we hold a snippet, not the page. (3) The instrumental study the grammar cites for its prosody claim, Lee Sook-hyang 2014 (Phonetics and Speech Sciences 6(4)), was downloaded open-access and read: it defines the Jejueo accentual phrase's basic pattern as <L+H L+Ha> 'like Seoul dialect' within the K-ToBI intonational hierarchy, i.e. phrase-level tonal prominence with no word stress or lexical pitch accent, which directly confirms the 'phrasal' coding and the the primary-stress rule. sources.citation: Lee, Sook-hyang (이숙향). 2014. 제주어 강세구의 억양 [The intonation patterns of accentual phrase in Jeju dialect]. 말소리와 음성과학 (Phonetics and Speech Sciences) 6(4): 117-123. doi:10.13064/KSSS.2014.6.4.117
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Abstract (p.117): 'The results showed that like Seoul dialect <L +H L+ Ha> pattern could be the basic pattern of accentual phase in Jeju dialect even though several differences were observed in the realization of each tone ... unlike Seoul dialect, most speakers showed <H L+ Ha> pattern in an accentual phrase beginning with a strong consonant.' Conclusion (p.122): '두 개의 실험을 통해 제주어 강세구의 억양기본패턴을 서울말과 같이 <L+H L+Ha>로 정의하였다' [Through two experiments the basic intonation pattern of the Jejueo accentual phrase was defined as <L+H L+Ha>, as in Seoul Korean]. Analysis is in the K-ToBI / Jun (1993, 2000
sources.note: Primary instrumental source behind the grammar's 'S.-H. Lee 2014' citation; establishes Seoul-type AP (L+H L+Ha) phrasal prosody with 15 speakers. downloaded now; should be added to the record as a supporting source.
